title: Coffee table
guidance: Four legs are notched on their outer faces to take the long aprons, which run the whole length and are themselves mortised for two cross rails. The end aprons are tenoned through the legs and the long aprons and wedged outside; the top is four planks whose outer boards are recessed over the legs' 8 mm locating tabs, and the planks lock together through the aprons and rails. The top lifts off as four planks and fans open; four triangular wedges, driven through the end aprons' tenons beside the legs, hold the frame tight and come out first. Each side then slides off the tenons as one unit and the long aprons lift out of the legs, which is how the frame's joinery is shown.

source.title: Coffee table

source.modifications: Designed in CadQuery; parts imported and assembled here, the outer top planks' leg pockets re-cut 10 mm outboard to seat the frame, four triangular wedges added to hold the end aprons tight, exploded and given the catalogue's paper-sunrise lighting
